summary.text: A random variable is a measurable function from a sample space of possible outcomes to a measurable space, and its range is typically a subset of the real numbers.
A discrete random variable takes finitely or countably many values, while a continuous one takes uncountably many, usually filling an interval.
Any random variable can be described by its cumulative distribution function, which gives the probability that it is less than or equal to a certain value.

facts.label: Usual notation
facts.value: Capital letters such as X, Y, Z and T

facts.label: One realization
facts.value: A particular outcome is called a random variate

facts.label: Early thinker
facts.value: Pafnuty Chebyshev, according to George Mackey

facts.label: Distribution
facts.value: Recording the probabilities of its outputs gives its probability distribution

facts.label: Values beyond numbers
facts.value: Words, graphs, vectors and even functions can be random

items.prompt: A statistics student says a random variable is simply a number that changes by chance. In the formal definition, what is it really?

options.label: A list of every outcome the experiment could produce
A measurable function from outcomes to a measurable space
The single outcome that happens when the trial is run
A probability measure placed on the sample space itself

items.explain: A random variable is defined as a measurable function from a sample space of possible outcomes to a measurable space.

items.prompt: A die can land on only six different faces. What kind of random variable describes one roll?

options.label: Discrete, with finitely many values
Continuous, with values filling an interval
Neither, since dice are not random
Both kinds at once

items.explain: When the range of a random variable is finite or countably infinite, it is a discrete random variable with a probability mass function giving a probability to each value.

items.prompt: A random variable is absolutely continuous. What is the chance it lands on one particular exact value?

options.label: A small positive chance
Exactly one half
Zero
One divided by the number of values

items.explain: Its distribution is described by a density that assigns probabilities to intervals, and each individual point must necessarily have probability zero.

items.prompt: You roll a die and it shows a 4. How would a mathematician describe that 4 in relation to the random variable?

options.label: The distribution of the variable
A particular outcome, or realization, of it
The sample space of the variable
The notation used for the variable

items.explain: A random variate is a particular outcome or realization of a random variable.

items.prompt: What does the cumulative distribution function of a random variable tell you?

options.label: The chance it is at most a certain value
The exact next value it will take
The number of times it was observed
The chance it equals its average

items.explain: It describes the probability that the random variable will be less than or equal to a certain value, and any random variable can be described this way.

items.prompt: Can a random variable take values that are not numbers, such as words or whole functions?

options.label: No, values must always be real numbers
No, only whole numbers are ever allowed
Yes, but only if the values are dates
Yes, values can lie in other sets, like words

items.explain: The definition is valid for any measurable space of values, so one can consider random elements such as words, vectors, graphs and functions.
